sections.title: Start Here
sections.subtitle: How to get the most from this workbook

blocks.text: You hold ninety days of momentum in your hands. This workbook is not meant to be read once — it is meant to be *written in*, week after week, until the plan in your head becomes a record on the page.

blocks.title: Before you begin
blocks.text: Set aside 30 minutes for the first session and 15 minutes every Sunday after that. Consistency beats intensity.
The rhythm

items: Complete the Vision pages once — this is your compass.
Set three 90-day goals using the goal worksheet.
Plan one week at a time in the weekly pages.
Close each month with the reflection prompts.

blocks.text: What you need

blocks.title: Your kit
items: A pen you enjoy writing with

blocks.text: A goal without a plan is just a wish.
Print single-sided on US Letter or A4. Every page is designed to be written on — the lines, boxes and tables are yours.

sections.title: Vision & Direction
sections.subtitle: Know where you are going before you plan the route

blocks.text: Answer these prompts quickly and honestly. First instincts are usually the truest. Write as much as you need — extra pages are at the back of each section.
If the next 90 days went perfectly, what would be different?
blocks.hint: Describe a normal day, ninety days from now.

blocks.text: What are you saying no to in order to say yes to this?
Which three words describe how you want to work this quarter?
Your compass statement
Combine your answers into one short statement you can pin above your desk.

blocks.title: Keep it visible
blocks.text: Photograph this page and set it as your phone wallpaper for the next 90 days.
Pick no more than three goals. For each one, name the milestone that proves progress and the deadline that creates urgency.

blocks.title: Guard your focus
blocks.text: Three goals is a ceiling, not a target. If everything is a priority, nothing is.
Milestone review dates

blocks.title: Goal hygiene
items: Each goal is written in one sentence.
Each goal has a visible progress measure.
Each goal has a date in the calendar, not just on paper.

sections.title: Weekly Planning Pages
sections.subtitle: Thirteen weeks, one page at a time

blocks.text: One page per week. Fill it in on Sunday evening or Monday morning — whichever moment you actually show up for.
What would make this week a win?
List the habits you are building this month. Tick each day you keep the promise — the streak is the reward.

blocks.title: Never miss twice
blocks.text: Missing one day is an accident; missing twice is the start of a new habit. Keep the streak alive.
Monthly review
What moved forward this month — and what evidence proves it?
What drained more energy than it returned?
What will you do differently next month?
We do not rise to the level of our goals; we fall to the level of our systems.
Open journal pages
Date & mood

sections.title: Closing Page
sections.subtitle: Before you turn the last sheet

blocks.text: What did you learn about yourself this quarter?
Write a note to yourself to open in 90 days.
blocks.hint: Be specific. Future-you will thank present-you.

blocks.text: End of workbook — the next one starts on page one. © 2026 Alex Mercer / Northline Press.
